title: Geo retry oscillation and model-variant mispair — incident follow-up and remediation plan
creator: Alex Chen
description: Summary: On 2026-02-27 22:14 UTC we observed a multi-region capacity event that triggered our smart-routing fallback logic. Multiple clients experienced increased latency and token errors for ~37 minutes. Root cause: an interaction between the geo-retry policy and a stale model-variant mapping cache. When a GC/eviction cycle removed a newly-rolled model-variant from regional lookup, the geo-retry attempted cross-region fallbacks but applied an outdated variant mapping; this produced repeated incompatible-variant fallback attempts and oscillatory reroutes between eu-west and us-east, amplifying load and causing downstream request timeouts. Impact: ~2.8% of hosted calls saw >3x latency, 0.6% resulted in structured error codes (VARIANT_MISMATCH) during the window. Several Dedicated customers in eu-west experienced degraded throughput due to excessive cross-region burst traffic.
mitigation: Immediate mitigation performed by on-call: 1) Quick rollback of the most recent variant-mapping config via config service (22:22 UTC) to stop oscillation. 2) Temporarily disabled cross-region geo-retries for impacted routes (22:25 UTC) to reduce amplification while mappings were reconciled. 3) Raised autoscaling headroom in eu-west by adding reserved burst instances for 45 minutes (22:30-23:15 UTC). Post-incident we re-enabled geo-retry with additional guardrails once mapping TTL and reconciliation checks were hardened.
root_cause_analysis: Contributing factors: (a) variant-mapping cache eviction did not trigger a validation/lookup on fallback paths which assume mapping consistency across regions; (b) geo-retry logic lacks a simple version/nonce check for variant compatibility before routing; (c) telemetry did not differentiate VARIANT_MISMATCH errors from model runtime errors in alerting rules, delaying operator diagnosis by ~6 minutes. Sequence: 22:13 capacity spike -> cache eviction of mapping shard -> geo-retry reads stale mapping -> attempts cross-region fallback to incompatible variant -> target region rejects with VARIANT_MISMATCH -> fallback triggers alternate region -> oscillation amplifies traffic -> timeouts and SLO breaches until rollback.
action_items: A1: Add variant-compatibility nonces to routing decisions so geo-retry only sends requests to variants that declare compatibility. Owner: Priya Nair. Due: 2026-03-18.
A2: Make mapping cache eviction emit high-priority telemetry and synchronous validation for active routes (fail closed). Owner: Diego Morales. Due: 2026-03-12.
A3: Extend geo-retry backoff with exponential jitter and a max cross-region attempts cap. Owner: Mina Park. Due: 2026-03-15.
A4: Update alerting rules to surface VARIANT_MISMATCH counts separately and add a runbook that includes immediate geo-retry disablement steps. Owner: SRE Team (oncall rotation). Due: 2026-03-10.
A5: Create an end-to-end chaos test that simulates mapping shard eviction + cross-region fallback to reproduce oscillation before release. Owner: QA/Eng reliability. Due: 2026-03-22.

A6: Add a canary gate in config rollout that prevents model-variant mapping changes from reaching multiple regions before intra-region validation passes. Owner: Feature-flagging team. Due: 2026-04-01.
A7: Post-incident customer outreach: Draft and send impacted-customer notes and SLA credit calculations. Owner: Customer Success (draft: Priya Nair). Due: 2026-03-05.
A8: Audit Dedicated autoscaling/burst rules to ensure cross-region bursts do not exhaust neighbor capacity during failover. Owner: Dedicated infra team. Due: 2026-03-20.
